lines.en: Let’s talk about “responsibility!”
: Aaaaaaaaah!!!
Rika Rokuhara was a normal middle-aged woman. And sure, she’d been arrested on several occasions for protesting and things of that nature. Sure, she wasn’t the brightest tool in the shed.
Sure, she’d give the occasional backroom handjob in exchange for concert tickets or VIP passes or, on one occasion, a large pizza. But none of that meant she didn’t understand responsibility!
: Why do I have to be responsible today?!
But that didn’t mean she couldn’t question when and why it would become relevant to her in day-to-day life.

: I’m not even a teacher. Why am I suddenly being given teacher-like responsibilities? Does this mean I can ask for a raise? Is this what it means to have a normal job? Why do I have so many questions?
: Why am I holding this clipboard? Why do I have to cover up my tattoos? Who killed Laura Palmer? Why won’t Rie answer any of my calls? These are all important things, Rika.
: But no, Rika! You have to read, Rika! You must teach!
She didn’t have to teach. In fact, all she had to do was head over to the soccer field and read off a list of contests that the girls of Class A would be competing in for this year’s Dorm Wars.
But she was such a mess that even this proved somewhat difficult. After all, where even was the soccer field? And why was it only called “soccer” in some countries?
She manages to steel herself, knowing full well that, despite how confused she was at the moment, she’d overcome this obstacle like she’d overcome so many things before.
Because yes, she was a normal middle-aged woman. She knew what it was like to raise a little girl and she knew the purpose of responsibility as a whole in the grand scheme of things.

But apart from this baseline understanding of one quality and “Ten Tips and Tricks to Make Even Straight Girls Want to Fuck You,” she wasn’t good at thinking of multiple things at once. And that made this hard.
Harder than it had to be. Because while she was tasked with opening up this year’s “ceremony,” she was also tasked with never doing anything to embarrass that same little girl she raised.
This was one more thing that added to her normalcy. Plenty of children out there want their parents to be as uninvolved as possible. And while that disappointed Rika, she understood it.
She just hoped that little girl would be able to forgive her for crossing paths with her before the final bell rang. And she would. For that little girl loved her mother too, after all.
But right — responsibility. Or, like they used to call it where I’m from, “weighing what you want to do against what you’re expected to do.”
When the weight of the world becomes too heavy, you’re often forced to shed some. So Rika’s choices at this point in time were “Do my job” or “Don’t interfere with Rin’s life.”
: What the hell is “death ball?”
But of course, she quickly forgot all of that the moment something else piqued her interest, eliminating both options entirely.
But that’s okay. Because responsibility only matters when there are people who expect something from you. But sometimes, different people expect different things.
Sometimes, you have to do something that’s going to upset someone.
Sometimes, there’s no right choice to make.
Sometimes, you have to take something that doesn’t belong to you.
But you stall and you cry and you stall some more until you throw yourself (or get thrown) on top of your niece’s friend on a roof somewhere and have to fuck her until she pops.
Sometimes, she goes away and it makes you sad. So you do sad things like wander around the city in hopes that there will be something that doesn’t remind you of her.
But everything does.
And nowhere is safe.
So while a normal middle-aged woman takes that one quality she can hold in her heart even deeper than the fingers of a bassist under some bleachers somewhere, you’re absent.
You have never cared about responsibility.
You are a failure.
And just because I can’t see you right now doesn’t make it any less true.
: No, really! The new stuff is great!
: Huh?
: It’s got the same vibe as the older stuff,  but the polish really shines and the production value as a whole is just way better. It’s super impressive, really.
: But anyway, here are the lockers! And right out there is the courtyard where I eat lunch sometimes. Oh,  and this over here is the gym!
: What the hell?
: Why is Noriko hanging out with a bunch of nerdy white guys?
: Noriko, don’t go in the gym! I’ve made this same mistake before! You’re better than this!
: Oh, and that crazy, hot lady is Rika. She’s my friend’s mom. She’ll go away if you don’t make eye contact with her.
After a brief off-screen explanation detailing why Noriko is giving a small group of white people a tour of the school, Rika makes her way to the soccer field.
Her clipboard also expands in size by roughly 50%%, but that’s an unimportant detail that you probably didn’t even realize until I pointed it out just now.
: So, uhh...hi!
: I know most of you have never talked to me before and probably don’t know who I am but, if you want to know who I’m definitely not, it’s Rin’s mom.
: Oh my fucking God.
: Looking good, Rika!
: Thanks, girl I definitely don’t know!
: Is it just me or does Rin’s mom have a really nice ass?
: Hm? Didn’t she just specifically say she ain’t Rin’s mom?
: Oh, Miku. Never change.
: Why are you here?! Where’s Imani?!
: Hello, other girl I don’t know! You are very pretty and probably very smart! Imani’s setting up the obstacle course right now, so she asked me to read off this year’s Dorm Wars thingy to everybody.
: Just drop it on the ground and one of us will read it. Thanks!
: But this part specifically states “Despite what Rin says, under no circumstances should you drop this on the ground and let anyone else read it.”
: Why?!
: I don’t know. Maybe there are some super secret details in it you’re not allowed to know?
: You...haven’t read it yet?
: Hah...Nice to meet you too, Rika...
: Miss Rokuhara, if you need any assistance regarding the reading of this year’s briefing, I’d be happy to lend a hand.
: Rokuhara? Ain’t that Rin’s last name too? No wonder she had to warn everybody they ain’t related. That’d confuse me too if I didn’t already know the truth.
: Nah, I’m good. Imani expects nothing but greatness from me, especially after learning how good I am at kissing. I will not let her down and have promised to read her words verbatim.
: Oh my God, stop!
: I will now read words to you!
: Ladies and other ladies, thank you for coming to this year’s annual Dorm Wars event! Even if it’s taking place during a school day that you were all obligated to attend.
: Given the lack of testosterone this year and the absence of the man you’d normally call the prize, I’ve decided to make things function a little differently.
: From what I understand, the Dorm Wars have been synonymous with individual competition over the last few years. With some minor exceptions like Makoto’s weird Sensei-guarding game.
: It wasn’t that-
: It is at this point that Makoto will interject about how it wasn’t that weird and you should say, “Shut up, Makoto.”
: Shut up, Makoto! I’m saying this because I have to, not because I want to!
: Now, direct your attention back to the clipboard and continue reading.
: While individual competition is fine and good, it’s counterintuitive to the entire point of sports day. Which is why, this year, a greater emphasis will be placed on teamwork.
: As such, I will not be assigning specific people to specific competitions and, instead, allow you girls to choose who will be competing in each event yourselves!
: Ourselves? But that means-
: Someone else will interject here and you will tell them there are caveats before an uprising takes place!

: Despite giving you the freedom to choose combatants yourselves, bear in mind that all students must participate in at least one competition! With the exception of Ami as her absence is already noted.
: Failure to adhere to this rule will result in a penalty of minus one point for each girl who does not participate.
: Oh, cool. This means I can abstain so long as we win a bunch of contests early. Good luck, Uta.
: Yumi’s not even here yet. So at this rate, you two might just cancel each other out.

: Let’s see, where was...right. As always, there will be a total of ten competitions for a total of ten points. But the majority of these competitions will be team-focused and require multiple participants.
: But seeing as not all of you are athletic, I’ve decided to throw a couple competitions into the mix that focus on other strengths so everyone will have an opportunity to compete.
: Additionally, the final two competitions of the SMUS-DDW: NBA - TEAaOKoSSEfBaB will not require you to choose your competitors.
: One of these will involve names being chosen from a hat and the other will be a special showdown between yours truly and the evil Wakana Watabe of Class B, who will be representing the first floor.
: Hell yeah! This means Imani is on our team! She likes us the most!
: It’s likely more due to the fact that Miss Watabe has been around for longer. Just as the first floor has-
: Blah, blah, blah. Imani is hot. Floor two wins.
: While Imani is, indeed, attractive, there is no one in this school more alluring than Miss Watabe. I would like to join the opposing team if possible, Miss Rokuhara.
: I’m willing to provide a physical bribe if need be.
: Hard pass.
: Are we going to learn what the competitions are ahead of time? Or is this a thing we’re just going to have to figure out once they come up?
: I think I can tell you them now. I just needed to get her “preamble” thingy out of the way since she says you guys are all really resistant to change.
: Wait! There’s a vital piece of information that’s yet to be revealed! The light at the end of the tunnel! The loot inside of the chest that is sports day!
: Translation: what’s the prize this year?
: She wrote “TBD.”
: One of these days, we’re gonna get an actual prize again.
: She says, not yet knowing she is going to be crushed under the weight that is the second floor.
: Your floor only weighs that much because of Touka’s boobs!
: That was entirely uncalled for, Miku!
: Besides, you have Futaba.
: And Ami and Sana and Maya and me! We’ve got a severe disadvantage here and I ain’t about to lose to boob weight!
: Can I read the competitions now or do we want to talk more about boobs?
: There’s only one way to truly discover which floor is the most boobalicious and it’s for all of us to-
: Ignore the whore and get back to the task at hand!
: I love it when you talk dirty to me, Chika.
: Man. You’re all horny as hell, aren’t you?
: Not all of us...
: Just the good ones.
: I couldn’t have said it better myself.
: No, but you could have made it way wordier and harder to understand.
: Yes, but so could Yasu and we all seem to love her.
: Love is but a delusional state of mind in relation to all but He who-
: Once Yasu begins to preach, things have gone too far. At that point, please read out the competitions regardless of the current conversational status. Roger.
: Competition one — egg toss. Two girls from each floor face off against one another to see who can keep their egg alive the longest.
: Competition two — trivia. A one-on-one return of everyone’s favorite knowledge-based competition that’ll serve as an opportunity to get non-athletes involved again.
: Competition three — obstacle course. Another one-on-one competition that’s sure to get the hearts of everybody pumping due to its crazy and quirky nature. Bring a weapon.
: Well, we’ve found Ayane’s competition.
: And...Tsuneyo’s...
: My entire body is a weapon. I will prove this once more today.
: Competition four — cheerleading. Two girls from each floor will team up to see who can form the best cheer. Please remember you are at school and keep most of your clothes on.
: Tch.
: Competition five — scavenger hunt. A sports day classic and the last one-on-one competition prior to the teacher showdown at the end.
: Competition six — relay race.
: Heck yeah! It’s finally my time to shine! No more of that fashion show nonsense!
: Awww but gyaru Miku was adorable and I miss her!
: Fast Miku is better! Y’all ain’t got a chance! Ya hear me?!
: I see you guys already understand what a relay race is, but I should probably let you know that one is going to be three-on-three.
: But, moving onto competition seven — death ball. There are currently no details about what death ball is. Please check back later.
: Well, that’s not worrying at all.
: Death is-
: Competition eight — the five-legged race.
: Five? Are you sure it’s not supposed to be the three-legged race?
: It says, “Not three!” in parentheses, so probably.
: Where...are we supposed to get the extra legs?...
: I’ll call my skull guy. He’ll know what to do.
: Competition nine — the newly-newlywed game.
: Wait, is that the game being randomly assigned to us?
: And what time is that starting exactly? I want to know when I should head back to the dorm.
: What even...is a newly-newlywed?
: Beats me, but it’ll sure make somebody happy with the amount’a bisexuals we’ve got up in here.
: Present.
: Present.
: Doing anything later, Chika?
: Yes, avoiding you.
: And competition ten — a very special teacher showdown featuring a classic party game while the night comes to an end.
: The following morning, we’ll reconvene and read out the results of the competition. But please be advised that there will be no unapproved “bonus contests” this year. There will be no exceptions.
: That is all.
: Hah...I love sports day, but this just feels wrong without Sensei. What good is a competition if we don’t have a handsome older man to choose which one of us is the winner?
: Yeah, I’m not doing this.
: What do you mean you’re not doing this? Didn’t you hear Rika? We’ll lose a point for every girl who doesn’t compete.
: Didn’t you hear the annoying, anti-social green-haired girl? She’s not going to compete either. Which means that even if Yumi and I don’t compete, we’ll only have a one-point disadvantage.
: But...we’re already down one girl with Ami being absent. And even if she’s excused, expecting seven of us to handle the rest of the competitions is putting way too much weight on our shoulders.
: Are you saying you aren’t up to the challenge?
: No, I’m saying I don’t understand why you’re trying to drop out before we’ve even distributed roles.
: Oh. Because I’m leaving.
: Leaving?
: Yeah. This sucks. I don’t want to be here anymore.
: Maya...you can’t just leave. The whole point of sports day is to work as a team. You’re really going to just...give us a handicap like that?
: That’s the plan, yeah. Besides, there’s something else I want to do instead.
: And what’s that? What’s more important than-
: You’re tired of waiting, aren’t you?
: Why now?
: Why would you wait until we’re all together to break off and follow your heart?
: I’m afraid I don’t know what you’re talking about.
: Maya, you know what I’m talking about. You can’t fool me.
: Right. Because...Past-Maya already explained to you how she felt or something, correct? And you’ve transplanted those feelings into Real-Maya. IE: me.
: I just don’t understand why it has to be now. You’ve had so many other chances.
: You don’t have to understand. You just have to cover for me and do your best to win all of the competitions while I go “follow my heart” as you so aptly put it.
: Because that’s what it is and you know it.
: Do I?
: What will you do if you find him?
: Who?
: What will you do if you find him?
: Would you believe me if I said I was going to ride him like a mechanical bull?
: Woah.
: You want honesty? There you go. Were you hoping for a different answer?
: I’m just...not used to hearing you be so open like that.
: And I’m not used to you prying personal details out of me like this.
: You’ve been acting weird lately, Ayane. And all of this gaslighting about how I’m not who I think I am and that you know so much about me is starting to get on my nerves.
: So please excuse me while I go confront a grown man and ultimately allow him to use my body like a sex toy.
: Peace.
: Oh, and good luck or whatever.
: Have fun.
: Well, I don’t like this one bit.
: Nodoka.
: Yes, my love?
: You’re staring at me an awful lot today.
: Am I?
: You sure are. And it’s starting to creep me out.
: You just seem...different. That’s all. More...depraved.
: Ah, thank you.
: Did something happen? A chance encounter on a long walk home? A secret rendezvous with a boy you met on the Internet? A girl perhaps?
: Why would I tell you even if any of that was true? It would just end up in a book.
: And that doesn’t excite you?
: Thank you very much.
: Otoha, from one creator to another, doesn’t the idea of being a part of something greater have some sort of appeal to you? I assumed you’d love simply being a character.
: For all you know, a young boy could stumble across my work accidentally and take great pleasure in your exploits.
: Mhm. Right. Or you could.
: And that’s a bad thing?
: Thank you very much.
: Anyway. As I was saying-
: Yeah, forget what you were saying. Why do people keep coming over here and handing you a sheet of paper?
: Whatever do you mean?
: You’re literally holding onto them. They’re right there.
: Otoha, you’re going to have to speak up. I can’t quite hear you.
: Nodoka, what are you planning this time? What is this?
: I’m not planning anything, Otoha.
: I’m just trying to give back to the community.
